[ There are smooth cubics for which it is true . For related problems see the section called “Stein manifolds”.]

evidence.quote: Problem 11.1.2 Let C be a smooth cubic in P2 . Then P2 \ C is algebraically parallellizable, but cannot be algebraically immersed in C2 . Can it be holomorhically immersed in C2 ? artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be a smooth cubic curve, and let $X = \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}) \setminus C$ be its complement. It is known that $X$ is algebraically parallelizable (its holomorphic tangent bundle is algebraically trivial) but admits no algebraic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^2$. For certain smooth cubics $C$, $X$ is known to admit a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^2$.

Question: Does there exist, for every smooth cubic curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$, a holomorphic immersion $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}) \setminus C \to \mathbb{C}^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on holomorphic embeddings and immersions of Stein manifolds (e.g., Forstnerič's 2017 survey) discuss related questions about immersing affine surfaces into $\mathbb{C}^2$, but no source located confirms a resolution for all smooth cubics. Partial results (immersions for special cubics, including cuspidal cubics, due to Nishimura and others) are known. The general question for arbitrary smooth cubics appears not to be definitively settled in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic embeddings and immersions of Stein manifolds: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known results on holomorphic immersions and embeddings of Stein manifolds, including affine complements in projective surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of holomorphically immersing complements of smooth cubics in $\mathbb{P}^2$ into $\mathbb{C}^2$ is discussed in the context of related open questions, with no definitive resolution stated.

status_evidence.title: Proper holomorphic immersions into Stein manifolds with the density property
status_evidence.snippet: Provides general criteria for holomorphic immersions of Stein manifolds; cites earlier work on special cubics by Nishimura giving explicit immersions for cuspidal cubics.
status_evidence.claim: Holomorphic immersions are known for some specific (e.g., cuspidal) cubics, but not stated for all smooth cubics.
